title: UK Met Office: El Niño Set to Be 'Strongest in Living Memory'
detail: The UK Met Office said the developing El Niño is on track to be the most intense in over a century, with sea-surface temperatures in the equatorial Pacific already more than 2°C above normal and forecast to exceed 3°C later in 2026 — well above the typical 1-2°C rise of a major event. Prof Adam Scaife, the Met Office's head of long-range forecasting, said: 'This is an unprecedented event. I have never seen an El Niño signal this intense in our forecasts.' Met Office climate scientist Dr Nick Dunstone said 2027 is 'very likely' to replace 2024 as the warmest year on record. Ocean temperatures at 100-meter depth are running roughly 8°C above normal in places, and the Met Office linked the event to already-visible impacts including below-average Indian monsoon rains and suppressed Atlantic hurricane activity.

media.caption: UK Met Office says the 2026 El Niño is set to be the strongest in over a century

title: Indonesia Wildfire Haze Chokes Malaysia's Sarawak, Shuts Nearly 600 Schools
detail: Indonesian authorities warned they would take legal action against anyone starting open fires as blazes on Borneo — more than 5,000 hotspots recorded by Indonesia's Forestry Ministry — cut visibility to as little as 1-10 meters in parts of Kalimantan and sent dense smoke across the border into Malaysia's Sarawak state. Sarawak recorded 'very unhealthy' air quality in one district and 'unhealthy' readings in eight others, prompting the closure of nearly 600 schools affecting about 200,000 students. Indonesia's fires have now burned roughly 285,000 hectares nationwide in 2026, up from the 107,000 hectares reported in mid-August, as the intensifying El Niño and prolonged dry season fuel the country's worst fire season in years.

media.caption: Haze from Indonesian wildfires forces school closures in Malaysia's Sarawak state
